1. Immutable V1.4 architecture (preserved)
All V1.4 evaluator, protection, and prohibition decisions in section 20 V1.4 remain binding. V1.5 adds
engineering topology only.
2. Component architecture
See machine-readable component_manifest.json. Summary: 23 components with explicit call graph and
write boundaries.
Rule:Domain evaluators MUST NOT call productive writers. Generic runner MUST NOT skip pre/post
gates.
3. Canonical end-to-end pipeline
VECTOR/CORPUS -> RUN REQUEST -> BINDING -> PRE-CONSTRAINT GATE ->
DETERMINISTIC REPLAY -> DOMAIN EVALUATOR -> METRICS+INVARIANTS ->
COMPARATOR -> PROTECTED DIGEST COMPARISON -> DELTA MANIFESTS ->
POST-CONSTRAINT GATE -> EVIDENCE BUNDLE -> EVIDENCE REGISTRY ->
PROMOTION EVIDENCE ADAPTER -> EXTERNAL GOVERNANCE
Each transition is specified inarchitecture_manifest.json with producer/consumer/forbidden reverse
direction.
4. Generic runner state machine
States: CREATED, BOUND, PRE_CONSTRAINT_CHECKED, REPLAY_READY, REPLAYED,
EVALUATED, COMPARED, DELTA_MANIFEST_BUILT, POST_CONSTRAINT_CHECKED,
EVIDENCE_BUILT, REGISTERED, FAILED.
Proofs: - Evaluators cannot bypass PRE_CONSTRAINT_CHECKED. - Promotion handoff requires
POST_CONSTRAINT_CHECKED PASS. - FAILED is terminal; no silent PASS. - Deterministic replay
required where CURRENT contracts guarantee determinism.
5. Domain evaluator contract
evaluate(context) -> DomainEvaluationResult
1

Context binds: run, baseline, candidate, corpus, config, data, seed, constraint, protected digest identities.
Result contains: domain, verdict, metrics, invariants, boundary_results, decision_deltas, seman-
tic_digest_deltas, evidence_refs, failure_classification.
No productive writes via this contract.
6. Machine-readable schemas
Full field specs incontract_schema_manifest.jsonfor: RunManifest, VectorManifest, CorpusManifest, Con-
straintMatrix, DomainEvaluationContext, DomainEvaluationResult, MetricResult, InvariantResult, Bound-
aryResult, ProtectedDigestManifest, DecisionDeltaManifest, RankingUniverseManifest, RankingDeltaMani-
fest, CapitalRiskCrsSizingEvidenceBundle, EvidenceBundle, PromotionEvidenceEnvelope.
7. Digest model
Algorithm SHA-256 over canonical JSON (sorted keys). Protected domains: ranking_universe and selection
separate.
Verdicts: DIGEST_EQUAL | DIGEST_CHANGED_EXPECTED | DIGEST_CHANGED_UNEXPECTED
| DIGEST_UNAVAILABLE | DIGEST_CONFLICTING.
UNEXPECTED -> fail-closed + WHOLE_SYSTEM_REPROOF.
8. Constraint matrix (build-ready)
Rows in constraint_matrix.json — includes RANKING_UNIVERSE->SELECTION with Cap2.3 sole
owner preserved.
9. Failure taxonomy
See failure_taxonomy.json. Failure classes bind to gvef.fan_out_reproof_resolver_v1 via
RESOLVER_TRIGGER_TAGS; reproof enum is never embedded ambiguously. EXECUTION_BLOCKED=true
for CURRENT_* classes. No failure class sets PROMOTION_ELIGIBLE=true.
10. Fan-out / reproof decision contract
Canonical enum only: LOCAL_EVALUATION, DOWNSTREAM_IMPACT_EVALUATION,
WHOLE_SYSTEM_REPROOF. See fan_out_reproof_matrix.json. Ambiguity escalates, never
downgrades.
11. Evidence lifecycle
GVEF authority ends atEVIDENCE_COMPLETE(EvidenceBundle REGISTERED + post gate PASS).
States through LIVE_ELIGIBLE areexternal governance.
12. Repository target structure
See architecture_manifest.json repo_paths. Reuse GHV scripts and governance ingress; no parallel
SSOT.

Appendix C — Normative Implementation Completeness & Reconciliation Rule
This appendix is normative and applies to every BWP, slice, component, contract, transition, gate, evaluator, digest,
manifest, registry, adapter, evidence object, failure mapping and authority boundary defined by this Blueprint. It does not
change blueprint_version=1.5, DESIGN_BASELINE=V1.4, or any existing architecture decision.
C.1 No implementation-by-presence assumption

The existence of a file, class, function, schema, test, manifest entry, configuration key, component name, prior PR, prior
evidence bundle, or COMPLETE/PASS flag MUST NOT be treated as proof that the Blueprint requirement is implemented.

Existing implementation MAY be reused only after exact reconciliation against the normative Blueprint requirement and
CURRENT repository truth.

A BWP MUST NOT be skipped solely because apparently matching implementation already exists.
C.2 Mandatory SOLL → IST → GAP → FIX → REPROOF sequence

SOLL: extract the complete normative requirement from this Blueprint and its referenced machine-readable manifests,
including fields, types, required/nullability rules, enums, values, defaults, identities, digests, ownership, call boundaries,
side effects, failure behavior, stop conditions, reproof class and safety prohibitions.

IST: inspect the CURRENT implementation and runtime/reachability evidence. Do not infer implementation from names or
documentation.

GAP: compare SOLL and IST explicitly. Every mismatch, omission, extra semantic behavior, unresolved ambiguity or
UNKNOWN is a gap until adjudicated.

FIX: implement only the proven missing or incorrect scope, preserving existing authority boundaries and reusing canonical
owners/SSOTs.

REPROOF: rerun the complete BWP acceptance surface and all affected upstream/downstream regression and
governance gates.
C.3 Exact implementation parity

Where the Blueprint specifies fields or values, closure requires exact field/value parity: names, types, requiredness,
nullability, enum domain, allowed values, defaults, nesting, serialization, digest binding, provenance and semantics.

Where the Blueprint specifies behavior, closure requires executable proof of that behavior: transitions, callers/callees,
ownership, failure classification, fail-closed behavior, fan-out/reproof routing, authority isolation and side-effect restrictions.

Where the Blueprint specifies a pipeline connection, component existence alone is insufficient; the intended producer →
consumer path and forbidden reverse direction must be proven.
C.4 UNKNOWN and ambiguity

UNKNOWN, UNPROVEN, PARTIAL, inferred compatibility, or name-only matches MUST NOT count as PASS.

If a normative requirement cannot be proven from CURRENT code/reachability/evidence, the BWP remains open or
fail-closed according to its stop condition.

Ambiguity in reproof scope escalates and never downgrades, consistent with Section 10.

19
C.5 Mandatory verification dimensions

Presence: required artifact/component/contract exists at the canonical owner path.

Structure: exact schema/API/configuration shape and machine-readable identity.

Values: required constants, enums, flags, defaults, digests, versions and bindings are exact.

Semantics: implementation meaning matches the Blueprint, not merely the identifier.

Wiring: required call graph, transition order, producer/consumer relationship and forbidden reverse paths are enforced.

Failure behavior: specified failure class, terminal/fail-closed behavior and reproof class are executable and tested.

Authority: no duplicated Selection, MV2, Risk, promotion or productive trading authority; GVEF authority remains as
defined.

Side effects: productive writeback, credentials, LIVE POST and PRE_EXTERNAL crossing remain prohibited unless
explicitly authorized outside GVEF.

Determinism/reproducibility: where required, repeated execution and serialization produce identical results under identical
bound inputs.

Regression: previously closed BWPs and protected semantic digests remain valid after the change.
C.6 BWP and slice closure rule

A BWP MAY be executed as one bounded work package containing multiple internal dependency slices. Slice boundaries
are proof/implementation boundaries, not independent authority domains.

A slice is PASS only when all requirements assigned to that slice are proven. A BWP is PASS only when every required
slice and the package-level acceptance gate are PASS.

One slice does not imply one PR. Prefer one coherent BWP PR unless a real dependency, review or gate boundary
requires otherwise.

A later BWP MUST NOT begin merely because predecessor artifacts exist; the predecessor must satisfy this
completeness rule and its own acceptance gate.
C.7 Test sufficiency

Existing tests MUST NOT be assumed sufficient. Their assertions must be reconciled against the complete normative
requirement.

Missing positive, negative, boundary, roundtrip, determinism, authority, failure-routing or regression tests required to prove
the Blueprint MUST be added within the owning BWP.

A green test suite proves only what it asserts. BWP closure additionally requires explicit coverage mapping from normative
requirements to implementation and proof.
C.8 Required closure evidence

Each BWP closure report MUST state the normative requirement count/surface, CURRENT implementation count/surface,
exact matches, gaps, UNKNOWNs, repairs, unresolved gaps, tests executed, regressions, governance gates, safety
counters and final verdict.

Closure requires: REQUIRED_UNKNOWN_CURRENT=0; REQUIRED_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT=0;
UNRESOLVED_GAP_COUNT=0; all BWP-specific acceptance criteria PASS; and all applicable safety invariants
preserved.

If zero code changes are required, the no-change conclusion itself must be supported by complete reconciliation evidence;
no artificial commit or PR is required.

If changes are required, governance impact/adjudication MUST be bound to the actual current diff and current PR head;
stale changed-path sets, hashes or prior-PR adjudications are invalid.
C.9 Global invariant
For this Blueprint, 'implemented', 'complete', 'PASS', 'build-ready', or equivalent closure language means proven
semantic implementation parity — not documentary presence. The burden of proof is on CURRENT implementation
and executable evidence. This rule applies retroactively to every BWP in the V1.5 sequence without renumbering or
changing blueprint_version=1.5.
End of Blueprint V1.5 normative completeness addendum — blueprint_version remains 1.5.
